title: Google Stock (GOOGL) Rises 0.8% to $282.44 (Nov 18)
summary: Alphabet (GOOGL) closed at $282.44 on Nov 18, up 0.80%, as the Nasdaq rose 0.42% and Anthropic, in which Google holds a stake, priced its IPO.
body_markdown:
Near its 52-week low. Alphabet closed 3.80% above its 52-week low and 30.88% below its 52-week high.


## Why Google Stock Rose


None of the reports reviewed for this article named a company-specific cause for Alphabet's gain on Wednesday. The stock moved with a firmer Nasdaq and finished slightly ahead of it, while the S&P 500 and the Dow declined.


The main Alphabet-related news came from Anthropic. On Wednesday, Anthropic priced its[initial public offering](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/learn/what-is-an-ipo/) at $83 per share, above the $70 to $78 range it set last week, and raised $81.3 billion, according to[CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/anthropic-ipo-ai-offering-price.html) . CNBC reported that Amazon and Google each own Anthropic stakes valued at over $100 billion, and that Google joined Microsoft, Nvidia and AMD in a group that agreed to invest $26 billion collectively at the IPO price.


As reported by[StockAnalysis](https://stockanalysis.com/news/anthropic-prices-ipo-83-per-share/) , Amazon and Google will together own about 28% of Anthropic after the deal. CNBC said the shares are expected to[begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/anthropic-ipo-nasdaq-debut/) .


## GOOGL Stock Analysis: Supporting Factors and Risks


### Supporting Factors


- Google Cloud revenue grew 103% to $30.7 billion in the third quarter, and the segment's operating income rose to $11.1 billion from $3.6 billion a year earlier, according to[Alphabet's third-quarter 2026 results release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652044/000165204426000080/googexhibit991q32026.htm) filed with the SEC.
- Total revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion, with Search and other revenue up 12% to $63.4 billion, per the same release.
- CNBC values Google's Anthropic stake at over $100 billion following the IPO pricing.


### Risks


- Capital expenditures reached $51.4 billion in the third quarter and $132.0 billion year to date, leaving quarterly free cash flow at negative $9.1 billion, per Alphabet's release.
- Alphabet repurchased no shares in the third quarter, compared with $11.5 billion a year earlier.
- Equity holdings can swing reported profit: the quarter included an $8.7 billion net loss on equity securities, which reduced net income by $6.7 billion.
